problems.title: Least common multiple and greatest common divisor
problems.question: Find lcm(18,15)+gcd(48,45).
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: $\operatorname{lcm}(a, b)=ab/\gcd(a, b)$.
steps: gcd(18,15)=3, so their lcm is 90. The second gcd is 3. Add them.

problems.title: Angles on a broken line
problems.question: In the printed diagram AB∥DE, ∠ABC=100° and ∠CDE=110°. Find ∠BCD.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Use a line through C parallel to AB and DE.
steps: BC makes 180°−100°=80° with the rightward horizontal. DC makes 110° with it. Their angle difference is 110°−80°.

problems.title: Remainder is a quarter of the quotient
problems.question: Divide 180 by a natural number d so the remainder is 25% of the quotient. Find the listed d.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: For the listed d=11, division gives q=16, r=4, satisfying r=q/4. The other listed divisors 12,13,9 give respectively remainders 0,11,0, which fail.

problems.title: Square a symmetric expression
problems.question: If $(a^2+b^2)/(ab)=3$, find $(a^4+b^4)/(a^2b^2)$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: Subtract 2 from 3².

problems.title: Distance equation on a line
problems.question: C is the midpoint of AB. How many points X on the full line satisfy 3XA=5(XB+XC)?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Scale to $A=0, C=1, B=2$. The equation becomes $3|x|=5(|x-2|+|x-1|)$.
steps: For x≤0, it gives x=15/7 outside that region. For 0≤x≤1, it gives x=15/13 outside that region. For 1≤x≤2, it gives x=5/3, valid. For x≥2 it gives x=15/7, valid.

problems.title: Two division points on a segment
problems.question: AC:CB=3:7 and BD:DA=7:8. If CD=14, find AB.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: CD=(8/15−3/10)AB=7AB/30. Set it equal to 14.

problems.title: Bisectors of supplementary angles
problems.question: Two same-side interior angles between parallel lines have bisectors making acute angles with the parallels in ratio 2:7. Find the smaller original angle.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The original angles sum to 180°, and their halves have the same ratio 2:7.
steps: The smaller original angle is 180·2/(2+7).

problems.title: Order three roots
problems.question: Order $a=2^{1/3}, b=3^{1/4}, c=5^{1/6}$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: For positive numbers, raising to power 12 preserves order.

problems.title: Mixing two alloys
problems.question: Zinc:copper ratios are 5:2 and 3:4 in two alloys. Their 28 kg mixture has equal zinc and copper. Find the first alloy mass.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: If its mass is x, zinc mass is $5x/7+3(28-x)/7=14$.
steps: Multiply by 7:5x+84−3x=98, so 2x=14.

problems.title: A system with infinitely many solutions
problems.question: For which k does 4x−3y=15+kx and x+2y=5k−kx have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The coefficient determinant is $2(4-k)+3(1+k)=11+k$.
steps: A zero determinant requires k=−11. At this k the coefficient rows are proportional with factor −2/3, but the constants 15 and −55 have ratio −11/3. Thus the equations are inconsistent rather than identical. For other k the solution is unique.

problems.title: Minimum divisor count
problems.question: Find the least number of positive divisors of $324k^3$ for prime k.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: If k=2 the count is (5+1)(4+1)=30. If k=3 it is (2+1)(7+1)=24. Any other prime gives 3·5·4=60.

problems.title: Read a straight-line graph
problems.question: Choose the equation of the drawn line, whose intercepts are (0,3) and (2,0).
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: Use y=mx+b with b=3.

problems.title: Square inside a triangle
problems.question: A triangle has base 8 and height 4. A square has one side on the base and two vertices on the other sides. Find its side.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: At height s the triangle width is $8(1-s/4)$ by similarity.
steps: Set this equal to the square side: s=8−2s, giving 3s=8.

problems.title: Nested radicals as absolute values
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt{x+2\sqrt{x-1}}+\sqrt{x-2\sqrt{x-1}}$ for x>2.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Put $t=\sqrt{x-1}>1$. The two radicands are $(t+1)^2$ and $(t-1)^2$.
steps: Their square roots are t+1 and t−1. Add them.

problems.title: Largest possible cancellation factor
problems.question: For natural n, find the largest possible gcd of 12n+3 and 5n+5.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Any common divisor divides $12(5n+5)-5(12n+3)=45$.
steps: Thus it is at most 45. At n=26, the numbers are 315 and 135, whose gcd is 45, proving attainability.

problems.title: Three filling rates
problems.question: Pumps 1+2 fill a pool in 35 minutes, 2+3 in 40, and 1+3 in 56. How long do all three take?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: The right side is (8+7+5)/280=1/14. Hence the total rate is 1/28 pool per minute.

problems.title: Distance from a parallelogram vertex
problems.question: A line through D has distances 4 and 7 from A and C of parallelogram ABCD. Find B’s distance.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: For signed distances to the line, $d_B=d_A+d_C$, since $B=A+C-D$ and $d_D=0$.
steps: If A, C are on the same side, the distance is 4+7=11. If they are on opposite sides, it is |7−4|=3. The only listed possibility is 11.
problems.note: The text does not specify on which sides of the line A and C lie, so it does not uniquely force 11.

problems.title: A double inequality
problems.question: Solve $-4\le1-(x-2)/3\le-3$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Subtract 1, multiply by −3 and reverse the inequalities.
steps: This gives 15≥x−2≥12, or 14≤x≤17.

problems.title: Largest integer in a set difference
problems.question: A=(−∞,7), B=[−4,6]. Find the largest integer in A\B.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: $A\setminus B=(-\infty,-4)\cup(6,7)$.
steps: The interval (6,7) has no integer. The greatest integer below −4 is −5.

problems.title: A reflected point on a line
problems.question: Reflect (3−a, a) across the x-axis. The result lies on y=2x+1. Find a.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The reflected point is $(3-a,-a)$.
steps: Substitute: −a=2(3−a)+1=7−2a. Thus a=7.

problems.title: An intermediate trapezoid width
problems.question: BC∥AD, AD=12, BC=4. A parallel section MN has AM:MB=3:5. Find MN.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The fraction of the way from AD toward BC is $t=3/8$. Width varies linearly.

problems.title: Incentre and a cyclic quadrilateral
problems.question: In triangle MNK, bisectors MA, KB meet at O, and A, N, B, O are concyclic. Find ∠N.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The incentre angle is $\angle MOK=90^\circ+\angle N/2$. Since OA, OB reverse OM, OK, $\angle AOB=\angle MOK$.
steps: In cyclic quadrilateral ANBO, opposite angles satisfy ∠AOB+∠ANB=180°. Thus 90°+N/2+N=180°, giving N=60°.

problems.title: Exactly one root of a radical inequality
problems.question: For which a does $(x-a)\sqrt{x+3}\le0$ have exactly one solution?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Domain $x\ge-3$. At $x=-3$ the product is always zero; for $x>-3$ require $x\le a$.
steps: If a≤−3, only x=−3 works. If a>−3, the entire interval [−3, a] works.

problems.title: Perimeter above a line through the incentre
problems.question: AB=5, AC=8. The parallel to BC through the incentre cuts AB, AC at M, N. Find perimeter AMN.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Let $BC=a$, altitude h and inradius r. Then $r/h=a/(a+5+8)$.
steps: Similarity gives scale (h−r)/h=13/(a+13). Multiply the original perimeter a+13 by this scale.

problems.title: Complete two squares
problems.question: Find x−y if $50x^2+4y^2-28xy+16x+64=0$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The left side is $(2y-7x)^2+(x+8)^2$.
steps: A sum of nonnegative squares is zero only if both are zero. Thus x=−8 and 2y=7x=−56, so y=−28.

problems.title: Seven integer points in a strict interval
problems.question: For which p does $|x|<p-1$ have exactly seven integer solutions?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The seven integers must be −3,−2,−1,0,1,2,3.
steps: To include ±3 require p−1>3. To exclude ±4 require p−1≤4. Combine them.

problems.title: Disjoint strict bounds
problems.question: For which a does the system .2x−4>.5x−8 and 6x−1>a+2 have no solution?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The bounds simplify to $x<40/3$ and $x>(a+3)/6$.
steps: There is no overlap exactly when (a+3)/6≥40/3, giving a+3≥80.

problems.title: Periodicity and oddness: check consistency
problems.question: f has period 2, is odd on $[-1,0)\cup(0,1]$, and $f(x)=1/(x-1)$ for −1≤x<0. Find f(9/2).
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: However, the endpoint data force f(−1)=−1/2, while oddness forces f(1)=1/2. Period 2 instead requires f(1)=f(−1). These conditions contradict one another.
problems.answer: Intended interior calculation: 2/3; strictly, no such function exists.
problems.note: The contradiction is at the included endpoints ±1. Excluding one endpoint from the oddness condition would repair the setup and preserve the intended calculation.

problems.title: Divide complex numbers
problems.question: Find $(\sqrt3-i)/(\sqrt3-2i)$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Multiply numerator and denominator by $\sqrt3+2i$.
steps: The numerator becomes 5+i√3, and the denominator is 3+4=7.

problems.title: A complex twentieth power
problems.question: Evaluate $(1+i\sqrt3)^{20}$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: $1+i\sqrt3=2(\cos(\pi/3)+i\sin(\pi/3))$.
steps: De Moivre gives modulus 2²⁰ and angle 20π/3, equivalent to 2π/3. Its cosine is −1/2 and sine √3/2.

problems.title: Check a complex cube root
problems.question: Choose a solution of $z^3+1-i=0$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: We need $z^3=-1+i$.

problems.title: A perpendicular line through an intersection
problems.question: Find the line perpendicular to AB, A=(2,2), B=(4,3), through the intersection of y=−x+8 and y=2x−1.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The AB slope is 1/2, so the perpendicular slope is −2.
steps: The two given lines meet where −x+8=2x−1, so x=3, y=5. The required line is y−5=−2(x−3).

problems.title: Similar triangles in a trapezoid
problems.question: In trapezoid ABCD, BC∥AD and ∠ABD=∠BCD. BC=2, BD=4, CD=3. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Also $\angle ADB=\angle DBC$ by parallel bases. Thus triangles ABD and DCB are similar.
steps: The scale is BD/BC=4/2=2. Therefore AB=2CD=6 and AD=2DB=8. Add 6+2+3+8.

problems.title: Two similar trapezoids
problems.question: A parallel cut divides a trapezoid of bases a, b into similar trapezoids. Find the cut length.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Corresponding base ratios give $a/x=x/b$.
steps: Thus x²=ab; choose the positive root for a length.

problems.title: Centroids of three smaller triangles
problems.question: Triangle ABC has perimeter 120 and centroid M. K, P, Q are centroids of ABM, BCM, CAM. Find perimeter KPQ.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
steps: Subtracting gives KP=AC/3, PQ=AB/3, QK=BC/3. Add them.

problems.title: Equality in the triangle inequality
problems.question: How many integer roots has $|2x-2.5|+|2x+4.2|=|2(-5)+3.3|$?
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: The right side is 6.7. The sum of distances to −4.2 and 2.5 has minimum 6.7, attained between those endpoints.
steps: Thus −4.2≤2x≤2.5, or −2.1≤x≤1.25. Its integers are −2,−1,0,1.

problems.title: Intersection of a cevian and a median
problems.question: BK:KC=2:1 on BC. AK meets median BM at O. Find AO:OK.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Assign masses $m_B=1, m_C=2$, giving $m_K=3$. Because M is midpoint of AC, take $m_A=m_C=2$.
steps: On segment AK the division ratio is opposite to endpoint masses: AO/OK=mK/mA=3/2.

problems.title: Simplify the supplementary radical expression
problems.question: Simplify $[8\sqrt a/(\sqrt a+7)-15\sqrt a/(a+14\sqrt a+49)]\div[(8\sqrt a+41)/(a-49)]+(7\sqrt a-49)/(\sqrt a+7)$.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Put $t=\sqrt a\ge0$, with $t\ne7$. Then $a+14\sqrt a+49=(t+7)^2$ and $a-49=(t-7)(t+7)$.
steps: The bracket becomes t[8(t+7)−15]/(t+7)²=t(8t+41)/(t+7)². Dividing by (8t+41)/[(t−7)(t+7)] leaves t(t−7)/(t+7). The last term is 7(t−7)/(t+7). Add and cancel t+7 to get t−7.

problems.title: A centroid-parallel chord and circle power
problems.question: A triangle inscribed in a circle has one side 21 cm. A chord through its centroid parallel to that side has portions outside the triangle of lengths 8 and 11 cm. Find the other two triangle sides.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Let the chord cut the two sides at D, E. Similarity at the centroid height gives $DE=(2/3)21=14$ and $AD/AB=AE/AC=2/3$.
steps: Power at D equates its chord-segment product to AD·DB. On the parallel chord the lengths are 8 and 14+11=25, so AD·DB=200. Since AD·DB=(2/9)AB², obtain AB²=900 and AB=30. At E the chord-segment product is 11(14+8)=242, hence (2/9)AC²=242 and AC²=1089, giving AC=33. The two sides may be named in the reverse order.

problems.title: A perpendicular through a bisector foot
problems.question: In isosceles ABC, AB=BC. The C-bisector meets AB at D. The perpendicular to CD at D meets line AC at F. Given AD=1 cm, find CF.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: Put $AB=BC=l$, $AC=b$, and $\theta=\angle C/2$. The bisector theorem gives $AD=lb/(l+b)$. The bisector-length formula is $CD=2lb\cos\theta/(l+b)$.
steps: Triangle CDF is right at D and its angle at C is θ, so CF=CD/cosθ=2lb/(l+b). Compare this with the expression for AD: CF=2AD.

problems.title: A pair of half-planes with no overlap
problems.question: Find a for which $y\ge(a-1)x-3a$ and $y\le(1-a^2)x-a-1$ have no common solution.
problems.idea: Use the definitions and retain all valid cases.
formulas: If the boundary slopes differ, their lines intersect, giving at least one solution. Thus require $a-1=1-a^2$, or $(a-1)(a+2)=0$.
steps: With equal slopes, no solution requires the lower y-bound to exceed the upper: −3a>−a−1, hence a<1/2. Of the two equal-slope values 1 and −2, only −2 qualifies. At −2 the bounds are y≥−3x+6 and y≤−3x+1, which are disjoint.
